back: Trachea: C-shaped rings. Bronchi: plates. Bronchioles and alveoli: none. Keeps airways open.
Goblet cells secrete mucus that traps particles; cilia sweep mucus up to the throat.

front: Function of smooth muscle in airways
back: Contracts or relaxes to change airway diameter and control airflow.

front: Function of elastic fibres in the lungs
back: Stretch during inspiration and recoil during expiration, helping to expel air.
A layer of very thin, flattened cells; forms alveolar walls, giving a short diffusion distance.

front: Features of an efficient gas exchange surface (alveoli)
back: Large surface area; thin barrier; steep gradients kept by ventilation and blood flow; moist.
Rate ∝ surface area × concentration difference ÷ thickness of the barrier.

front: How to recognise a bronchiole in a section
back: No cartilage; ring of smooth muscle; folded lumen; ciliated or cuboidal lining.
The gap at the back lets the oesophagus expand during swallowing.
